fields.description: Upsert key, same idea as LLM Usage Log keyed by Bifrost's log ID — re-polling an already-known failed job updates last_seen instead of creating a duplicate row. Purely a historical/drill-down table — no alerting logic of its own; Frappe Worker Health Log's failed_job_count/failed_job_critical_streak is what actually drives the Failed Job Threshold alert.
fields.label: RQ Job ID

fields.description: The enqueued method's dotted path (rq's job.func_name), e.g. frappe.email.queue.flush. Root input to failure_signature below — not shown as a standalone filter, just grouping material.
fields.label: Job Name

fields.description: Set once, on first upsert of this rq_job_id.
fields.label: First Seen

fields.description: Updated every poll the job still appears in RQ's FailedJobRegistry.
fields.label: Last Seen

fields.description: Set true when the job ID no longer appears in FailedJobRegistry on a subsequent poll (requeued, manually cleared, or expired out) — distinguishes "silently disappeared" from "still actively failing", both of which matter operationally.
fields.label: Resolved

fields.description: Exception class name, parsed server-side from the last line of exc_info (e.g. "KeyError" from "KeyError: 'foo'"). "Unknown" if that line doesn't match the usual traceback format.
fields.label: Exception Type

fields.description: sha256(exc_type + "::" + job_name), truncated to 16 hex chars — the dashboard's root-cause grouping key. Two failures with the same exception type from the same method collapse into one group, across hosts and over time.
fields.label: Failure Signature

fields.description: Raw traceback string from RQ, as sent by the agent.
fields.label: Exception Info
